answer: Through the nadir, the economy stays open to anyone willing to pay the price of entry, and closed to free clones. Before earning, each identity must complete a verifiable delay function — a computation that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be sped up with more hardware. The lotus gate makes time the currency: a thousand clones need a thousand sequential waits, and no amount of parallel machines shortens a single wait. That is the point of the hollow: cloning stops paying the moment each copy costs as much as the original.
